- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true +15%), apply mean reversion bias: subtract 2–5% from next 3 periods to prevent overhang.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.2–0.8) and forecast deviates >5% from true, adjust toward historical 30-day mean of prior 10 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), reduce forecast by 3–5% for next period to reflect lagged momentum.
- When sentiment history shows repeated volatility (e.g., alternating +/–0.5+), apply smoothing: forecast = 0.7×previous + 0.3×current sentiment-weighted average.
